feasibility_analysis.title: React Native Components vs MUI Components - Feasibility Analysis
feasibility_analysis.conclusion: ✅ FULLY FEASIBLE - React native components and MUI components can be used interchangeably in JSX

details.notes: Native components use standard HTML attributes (className, style, onClick, etc.). MUI components accept both standard props and MUI-specific props (sx, variant, etc.). Both work seamlessly together.
Native components can use inline styles, className with CSS, or be wrapped in MUI Box with sx prop. MUI components use sx prop for theme-aware styling. Both approaches can coexist.

details.explanation: Both native and MUI components use the same React event handlers (onClick, onChange, etc.). Event handling is identical.

details.notes: Native components require no imports (they're built into React). MUI components require imports from '@mui/material'. Both can be used in the same file without conflicts.

details.explanation: Both native and MUI components have full TypeScript support. Native components use React's built-in types, MUI components have their own type definitions.

example_code.description: Example showing seamless mixing of native and MUI components

recommendations: Use MUI components when they provide better functionality or styling
Use native components for simple elements that don't need MUI features
Wrap native components in MUI Box when you need MUI styling utilities
Mix both types freely - they work identically in JSX

mixing_components.title: Mixing Native and MUI Components
mixing_components.description: React native components and MUI components can be used seamlessly together in the same component.
rules: Native components require no imports - they're built into React
Both types can be nested within each other
Both types use the same JSX syntax and event handlers
Native components use standard HTML attributes (className, style, onClick)
MUI components accept both standard props and MUI-specific props (sx, variant)

native_components: Use inline styles: style={{ width: 100, height: 100 }}
Wrap in MUI Box for theme-aware styling:
mui_components: Use sx prop for theme-aware styling: sx={{ width: 100, height: 100 }}
Use variant prop for predefined styles: variant="contained"
Use theme system for consistent styling

when_to_use_native: Simple elements that don't need MUI features (img, div, input type='date')
When you want to minimize dependencies
When native HTML provides sufficient functionality
when_to_use_mui: When you need Material Design styling
When you need advanced component features
For complex interactive components (Button, TextField, Menu)
